acidic.description: Low-pH foods and drinks (roughly pH below 4). Especially relevant for laryngopharyngeal reflux (LPR), where acid and pepsin exposure irritate the throat.

caffeine.description: Caffeinated drinks and foods; caffeine may lower lower-esophageal-sphincter pressure in some people.

mint.description: Peppermint and spearmint may relax the lower esophageal sphincter in some people.

alcohol.description: Alcoholic drinks; wine and spirits are commonly reported reflux triggers.

carbonation.description: Carbonated drinks can distend the stomach and are also acidic.

high_fat.description: Fatty or fried foods slow stomach emptying and may lower sphincter pressure.

spicy.description: Spicy foods can trigger heartburn symptoms in some people.

chocolate.description: Chocolate contains methylxanthines and fat and is a commonly reported trigger.

raw_garlic_onion.description: Raw garlic and onion are commonly reported triggers; cooked forms are usually better tolerated.

large_portion.description: Very large meals distend the stomach and increase reflux episodes; eating close to bedtime adds to the effect.
